# Campeyyakkhandhaka (Kd 9)
**ID:** Kd 9
**Section:** Khandhaka (kd)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Campeyyakkhandhaka
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-kd9
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m2.mul8.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Campeyyakkhandhaka* is the ninth chapter of the *Mahāvagga* in the Khandhaka division of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [Frauwallner 1956; von Hinüber 1996; Norman 1983]. In the *Cullavagga* account of the Second Council at Vaiśālī, the text is also cited as the *Campeyyaka Vinayavatthu* [von Hinüber 1996; Sung 1999]. Often translated as "The chapter on legal procedures" or "On (the monks at) Campā" [SuttaCentral; Norman 1983], it provides a detailed, technical treatment of monastic jurisprudence and the formal validity of communal ecclesiastical acts (*saṅghakamma*) [SuttaCentral; von Hinüber 1996]. The narrative begins at Campā when the monk Kassapagotta is maliciously accused of having committed an offense, prompting the Buddha to lay down criteria distinguishing valid procedures from invalid or discordant acts carried out by an incomplete or factional assembly; violations incur an offense of wrongdoing (*dukkaṭa*) [SuttaCentral; Entrance to the Vinaya 1983; Banerjee 1979; Horner 1966].
The text corresponds functionally to the *Karmavastu* found in Northern Buddhist traditions [Frauwallner 1956; Prebish 1994; SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral identifies full parallels in the Sanskrit Mūlasarvāstivāda *Karmavastu*, Tibetan Mūlasarvāstivāda *Campeyya*, and Chinese translations of the Mūlasarvāstivāda, Sarvāstivāda, Dharmaguptaka, and Mahīśāsaka Vinayas [SuttaCentral]. Banerjee notes that the introductory narrative in the Tibetan Vinaya closely mirrors the Pali account—with the accused monk named Sde-’joms (Senajit) corresponding to Kassapagotta—though the Pali procedural discussions are more extensive [Banerjee 1979]. DharmaNexus confirms strong cross-language alignment between this text and the Sanskrit *Karmavastu* (SA_K01_vinv10_u) and Tibetan *Vinayavastu* [DharmaNexus]. Internally, DharmaNexus records extensive text reuse with other legal and procedural texts of the Vinaya, most prominently the *Kammakkhandhaka* (Kd 11), *Samathakkhandhaka* (Kd 14), *Pavāraṇākkhandhaka* (Kd 4), and *Pañcavagga* (Pvr 21), in addition to shared formulaic material with the *Bhaddāli Sutta* (MN 65) [DharmaNexus]. Complete English translations have been made by T. W. Rhys Davids and Hermann Oldenberg, I. B. Horner, and Bhikkhu Brahmali [Prebish 1994; SuttaCentral].

- Full parallels (SuttaCentral): san-mu-kd10 Karmavastu; xct-mu-kd10 Campeyya; lzh-mu-kd10 Campeyya; Lzh Sarv Kd10 Campeyya Khandhaka; Lzh Dg Kd 10 Campeyya Khandhaka; Lzh Mi Kd 10c c. Campeyya Khandhaka
- Resembling parallels (SuttaCentral): Lzh Mg Bu Pn1 Vagga 1. Upasampadā; Kd 22 Sattasatikakkhandhaka; Kd 12 Pārivāsikakkhandhaka
- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Kammakkhandhaka (Kd 11) (§7.14.82.1_0–7.14.86 ↔ §35.1.19_0–35.1.25); Samathakkhandhaka (Kd 14) (§2.2.3_6–2.2.16 ↔ §1.1.6–1.1.17); Bhaddāli Sutta (MN 65 (PTS MN i 437)) (§1.9.5–2.1.0 ↔ §13.5–14.1); Pavāraṇākkhandhaka (Kd 4) (§2.4.1–3.1.0 ↔ §3.2.3–3.3.0); Vinayapiṭake Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā (Tika Vin05t) (§6.4.4–6.4.17 ↔ §1327_2–1327_12); Pañcavagga (Pvr 21) (§6.4.21–6.4.35 ↔ §2.3–2.16); Mahākhandhaka (Kd 1) (§1.7.6–1.7.13 ↔ §31.3.3–31.4.5); Vinayapiṭake Khuddasikkhā-mūlasikkhā (Tika Vin13t) (§3.3.3–3.3.7 ↔ §1972_1–1972_5)

**Sources**

- [SuttaCentral] SuttaCentral entry for pli-tv-kd9 — Supplied title, blurb on Kassapagotta and saṅghakamma, modern translations, and parallel texts.
- [DharmaNexus] DharmaNexus text-reuse database — Supplied cross-linguistic alignments with the Karmavastu and internal Pali reuse data.
- [Frauwallner 1956] E. Frauwallner, The Earliest Vinaya and the Beginnings of Buddhist Literature (1956) — Outlined the position of Campeyyakkhandhaka in the Khandhaka sequence corresponding to Karmavastu.
- [Entrance to the Vinaya 1983] Entrance to the Vinaya: Vinayamukha Vol. 3 (1983) — Discussed the prohibition at Campā against performing saṅghakamma with incomplete attendance and the resulting dukkaṭa penalty.
- [von Hinüber 1996] Oskar von Hinüber, A Handbook of Pāli Literature (1996) — Described the text's placement in Mahāvagga, its alternative name Campeyyake vinayavatthusmiṃ, and technical legal content.
- [Horner 1966] I. B. Horner, The Book of the Discipline, Vol. VI (1966) — Confirmed the class of offense incurred in Mahāvagga IX as wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
- [Norman 1983] K. R. Norman, Pāli Literature (1983) — Listed the text among Khandhaka chapters as 'On (the monks at) Campā'.
- [Banerjee 1979] Anukul Chandra Banerjee, Sarvāstivāda Literature (1979) — Analyzed correspondence between the Tibetan vinaya text and the Pali Campeyyakkhandhaka, noting Kassapagotta/Sde-hjoms.
- [Prebish 1994] Charles S. Prebish, A Survey of Vinaya Literature (1994) — Listed the text, its Karmavastu counterpart, and translations by Horner and Rhys Davids/Oldenberg.
- [Sung 1999] Kang-yuan Sung, Tradition and Development in the Mo-ho-sêng-ch'i-lü (1999) — Noted the reference to 'Campeyyaka vinayavatthu' in the Sattasatikakkhandhaka.
